sources.rawExcerpt:
Basic Ragù Bolognese | Daniel Gritzer | Serious Eats
Source timing: total225minutes; cook225minutes; yield2quarts;16servings.
INGREDIENTS
2 packets unflavored powdered gelatin (1/2 ounce; 15 g)
2 cups homemade or store-bought low-sodium broth (475 ml)
3 tablespoons (45 g) unsalted butter
2 large carrots (about 375 g; 12 ounces), peeled and finely minced
3 medium celery ribs (about 240 g; 8 ounces), finely minced
2 medium yellow onions (about 480 g; 1 pound), finely minced
4 pounds (1.8 kg) ground meat, either all beef or 2 pounds beef with 1 pound each ground pork and veal, divided
1/4 cup (60 ml) tomato paste
1 1/2 cups (350 ml) dry white or red wine
2 bay leaves
Kosher salt
Pinch freshly grated nutmeg
1/2 teaspoon (3 ml) Asian fish sauce
1/2 cup (120 ml) heavy cream
METHOD (all operational details reexpressed, not untouched HTML)
1. Put the broth in a wide container, distribute the powdered gelatin over its surface, and set it aside to hydrate.
2. In a large Dutch oven, melt butter at medium-high heat until foamy. Add the finely minced carrots, celery and onions. Stir while cooking about 6 minutes, until they become translucent. Add only half of the ground meat (2 pounds). Cook about 15 minutes, occasionally stirring and breaking apart large clumps, until the pot bottom develops pronounced browning.
3. Add the remaining 2 pounds ground meat. Stir, scrape the browned pot bottom, and break this addition into very fine pieces. Continue about 6 minutes, until all meat has cooked through. Reduce heat whenever necessary to avoid scorching.
4. Stir in tomato paste and cook with stirring for 2 minutes. Pour in wine, scraping the bottom, and bring it to a boil. Cook about 5 minutes so the raw alcohol odor disappears, then add both bay leaves.
5. Add the set-aside broth, including every bit of hydrated gelatin scraped from its container. Bring to a simmer, then lower heat so the simmer is very gentle. Add salt, the pinch of freshly grated nutmeg and fish sauce. Simmer around 3 hours with occasional stirring, until the sauce is thick and essentially no surplus liquid remains. Skim surface fat, discard it and remove the bay leaves. Stir in heavy cream, then adjust salt to taste.
6. Use the sauce immediately, or keep it refrigerated for up to 5 days, or frozen for up to 3 months.
